64	
65	GENESIS_HASH = bytes(32)
66	_DOMAIN = b"auditchain/entry/v1"
67	_INDEX_BYTES = 8
68	
69	# Self-describing envelope of AuditLog.encrypt / decrypt_entry:
70	# magic, one-byte algorithm id (0x01 == AES-256-GCM), 12-byte nonce, then the
71	# AESGCM output (ciphertext || 16-byte authentication tag).
72	_ENC_MAGIC = b"auditchain/encrypted-entry/v1\0"
73	_AAD_DOMAIN = b"auditchain/aead/v1\0"
74	_ALG_AES256_GCM = 0x01
75	_KEY_BYTES = 32
76	_NONCE_BYTES = 12
77	_GCM_TAG_BYTES = 16
78	
79	_LEAF_DOMAIN = b"auditchain/merkle-leaf/v1"
80	_NODE_DOMAIN = b"auditchain/merkle-node/v1"
81	_EMPTY_DOMAIN = b"auditchain/merkle-empty/v1"
82	
83	_AUTH_DOMAIN = b"auditchain/auth/v1"
84	_EVOLVE_DOMAIN = b"auditchain/key-evolve/v1"
85	_LOCATE_DOMAIN = b"auditchain/locate/v1"
86	# HMAC keyed by the caller-supplied encryption key, locating encrypted
87	# entries by their original plaintext. HMAC (rather than a plain hash) keeps
88	# the locator unguessable without the key; the index stores only these
89	# digests, never the plaintext or the key.
90	_ENC_LOCATE_DOMAIN = b"auditchain/encrypted-locate/v1\0"
91	
92	# Binary framing of encode_audit_receipt / decode_audit_receipt: a fixed
93	# magic, then unsigned 8-byte big-endian integers and length-prefixed blobs.
94	_RECEIPT_MAGIC = b"auditchain/audit-receipt/v1\0"
95	# Binary framing of encode_audit_batch / decode_audit_batch: same u64/blob
96	# rules, one shared proof at the end instead of one proof per item.
97	_BATCH_MAGIC = b"auditchain/batch/v1\0"
98	_BATCH_VERSION = 1
99	_U64_BYTES = 8
100	_U64_LIMIT = 1 << 64
101	
102	# Signed snapshot-root checkpoint of AuditLog.sign_root / verify_signed_root.
103	# An Ed25519 signature over the hash algorithm, snapshot size, Merkle root and
104	# chain head; the signing seed is supplied per call and never stored.
105	_SIGNED_ROOT_DOMAIN = b"auditchain/signed-root/v1\0"
106	_SIGNED_ROOT_VERSION = 1
107	_ED25519_KEY_BYTES = 32
108	_ED25519_SIGNATURE_BYTES = 64
109	
110	# Binary framing of encode_signed_audit_batch / decode_signed_audit_batch:
111	# a fixed magic, then the envelope version as a u64 and two u64-length-prefixed
112	# blobs holding the complete canonical encode_audit_batch and
113	# encode_signed_root bytes, in that order and with nothing else.
114	_SIGNED_AUDIT_BATCH_MAGIC = b"auditchain/signed-audit-batch/v1\0"
115	_SIGNED_AUDIT_BATCH_VERSION = 1
116	
117	# Stages are encoded as 8-byte big-endian integers inside tags.
118	_MAX_STAGE = 1 << 64
119	
120	
121	def _digest_size(hash_name: Any) -> int:
122	    """Fixed digest width of ``hash_name`` in bytes.
123	
124	    Only hashlib algorithms with a fixed-length digest are accepted: a
125	    non-str name raises TypeError, an unknown algorithm or one without a
126	    fixed-length output (e.g. the SHAKE XOFs, whose ``digest_size`` is 0)
127	    raises ValueError.
128	    """
129	    if not isinstance(hash_name, str):
130	        raise TypeError("hash_name must be a string")
131	    try:
132	        digest_size = hashlib.new(hash_name).digest_size
133	    except ValueError as error:
134	        raise ValueError(f"unknown hash algorithm: {hash_name}") from error
135	    if digest_size == 0:
136	        raise ValueError(
137	            f"hash algorithm {hash_name!r} has no fixed-length digest"
138	        )
139	    return digest_size
140	
141	
142	def _as_bytes(payload: Any) -> bytes:
143	    if isinstance(payload, bytes):
144	        return payload
145	    if isinstance(payload, bytearray):
146	        return bytes(payload)
147	    if isinstance(payload, str):
148	        return payload.encode("utf-8")
149	    raise TypeError("payload must be bytes, bytearray or str")
150	
151	
152	def _check_key(key: Any) -> bytes:
153	    if not isinstance(key, bytes):
154	        raise TypeError("key must be bytes")
155	    if len(key) != _KEY_BYTES:
156	        raise ValueError(f"key must be {_KEY_BYTES} bytes")
157	    return key
158	
159	
160	def _check_nonce(nonce: Any) -> bytes:
161	    if not isinstance(nonce, bytes):
162	        raise TypeError("nonce must be bytes")
163	    if len(nonce) != _NONCE_BYTES:
164	        raise ValueError(f"nonce must be {_NONCE_BYTES} bytes")
165	    return nonce
166	
167	
168	def _load_ed25519_seed(private_key: Any) -> Ed25519PrivateKey:
169	    """Load a 32-byte Ed25519 private key seed; the seed is never stored."""
170	    if not isinstance(private_key, bytes):
171	        raise TypeError("private_key must be a 32-byte Ed25519 seed")
172	    if len(private_key) != _ED25519_KEY_BYTES:
173	        raise ValueError(
174	            f"private_key must be {_ED25519_KEY_BYTES} bytes (an Ed25519 seed)"
175	        )
176	    return Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(private_key)
177	
178	
179	def _load_ed25519_public(public_key: Any) -> Ed25519PublicKey:
180	    if not isinstance(public_key, bytes):
181	        raise TypeError("public_key must be a 32-byte Ed25519 public key")
182	    if len(public_key) != _ED25519_KEY_BYTES:
183	        raise ValueError(
184	            f"public_key must be {_ED25519_KEY_BYTES} bytes (an Ed25519 public key)"
185	        )
186	    return Ed25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes(public_key)
187	
188	
189	def _signed_root_message(hash_name: str, size: int, root: bytes, head: bytes) -> bytes:
190	    """M of sign_root / verify_signed_root.
191	
192	    ``D || 0x01 || B(UTF-8(hash_name)) || U(size) || B(root) || B(head)``
193	    with ``D = b"auditchain/signed-root/v1\\0"``, ``U`` an unsigned 8-byte
194	    big-endian integer and ``B(x) = U(len(x)) || x``.
195	    """
196	    return (
197	        _SIGNED_ROOT_DOMAIN
198	        + bytes((0x01,))
199	        + _encode_blob(hash_name.encode("utf-8"))
200	        + _encode_u64(size, "size")
201	        + _encode_blob(root)
202	        + _encode_blob(head)
203	    )
204	
205	
206	def _seal_aad(index: int, previous_hash: bytes) -> bytes:
207	    return (
208	        _AAD_DOMAIN
209	        + bytes((_ALG_AES256_GCM,))
210	        + index.to_bytes(_INDEX_BYTES, "big")
211	        + previous_hash
212	    )
213	
214	
215	def _seal_envelope(nonce: bytes, sealed: bytes) -> bytes:
216	    return _ENC_MAGIC + bytes((_ALG_AES256_GCM,)) + nonce + sealed
217	
218	
219	def _parse_envelope(payload: Any) -> tuple[int, bytes, bytes]:
220	    """Split an encrypted-entry envelope into ``(algorithm, nonce, sealed)``."""
221	    if not isinstance(payload, (bytes, bytearray)):
222	        raise TypeError("entry.payload must be bytes")
223	    material = bytes(payload)
224	    if not material.startswith(_ENC_MAGIC):
225	        raise ValueError("payload is not an auditchain encrypted-entry envelope")
226	    offset = len(_ENC_MAGIC)
227	    try:
228	        algorithm = material[offset]
229	    except IndexError:
230	        raise ValueError("truncated envelope: missing algorithm byte") from None
231	    offset += 1
232	    if algorithm != _ALG_AES256_GCM:
233	        raise ValueError(f"unsupported encryption algorithm: {algorithm:#04x}")
234	    nonce_end = offset + _NONCE_BYTES
235	    if len(material) < nonce_end:
236	        raise ValueError("truncated envelope: missing nonce")
237	    nonce = material[offset:nonce_end]
238	    sealed = material[nonce_end:]
239	    if len(sealed) < _GCM_TAG_BYTES:
240	        raise ValueError("truncated envelope: ciphertext must include a 16-byte tag")
241	    return algorithm, nonce, sealed
242	
243	
244	def entry_digest(index: int, previous_hash: bytes, payload: bytes, *, hash_name: str = "sha256") -> bytes:
245	    """Digest binding an entry to its position and predecessor."""
246	    if not isinstance(index, int) or index < 0:
247	        raise ValueError("index must be a non-negative integer")
248	    digest_size = _digest_size(hash_name)
249	    previous = bytes(previous_hash)
250	    if len(previous) != digest_size:
251	        raise ValueError(f"previous_hash must be {digest_size} bytes")
252	    digest = hashlib.new(hash_name)
253	    digest.update(_DOMAIN)
254	    digest.update(index.to_bytes(_INDEX_BYTES, "big"))
255	    digest.update(previous)
256	    digest.update(bytes(payload))
257	    return digest.digest()
258	
259	
260	def decrypt_entry(entry: Any, key: Any, *, hash_name: str = "sha256") -> bytes:
261	    """Decrypt an entry produced by :meth:`AuditLog.encrypt`.
262	
263	    Validates, in order, that ``entry`` is an :class:`Entry` with a
264	    well-formed encrypted-entry envelope, that ``key`` is 32 ``bytes``, that
265	    ``entry.entry_hash`` equals :func:`entry_digest` over the envelope at the
266	    entry's position, and finally the AES-256-GCM authentication tag with the
267	    same AAD used when sealing (``b"auditchain/aead/v1\\0" || 0x01 || index
268	    (u64 big-endian) || previous_hash``). Only then is the plaintext
269	    returned; plaintext encoding rules are the same as for :meth:`AuditLog.append`
270	    — callers receive exactly the bytes appended (a ``str`` comes back as its
271	    UTF-8 encoding). Type errors raise TypeError; a bad key length, a plain
272	    or malformed envelope, an unknown algorithm, an entry-digest mismatch or
273	    failed AEAD authentication raise ValueError. The call is read-only and
274	    never mutates the entry or a log.
275	    """
276	    if not isinstance(entry, Entry):
277	        raise TypeError("entry must be an Entry")
278	    if not isinstance(hash_name, str):
279	        raise TypeError("hash_name must be a string")
280	    _check_key(key)
281	    if not isinstance(entry.index, int) or isinstance(entry.index, bool):
282	        raise TypeError("entry.index must be an integer")
283	    if entry.index < 0 or entry.index >= (1 << 64):
284	        raise ValueError("entry.index is out of range for the entry framing")
285	    if not isinstance(entry.previous_hash, (bytes, bytearray)):
286	        raise TypeError("entry.previous_hash must be bytes")
287	    if not isinstance(entry.entry_hash, (bytes, bytearray)):
288	        raise TypeError("entry.entry_hash must be bytes")
289	    _, nonce, sealed = _parse_envelope(entry.payload)
290	    digest_size = _digest_size(hash_name)
291	    previous_hash = bytes(entry.previous_hash)
292	    if len(previous_hash) != digest_size:
293	        raise ValueError(f"entry.previous_hash must be {digest_size} bytes")
294	    expected_hash = entry_digest(
295	        entry.index,
296	        previous_hash,
297	        bytes(entry.payload),
298	        hash_name=hash_name,
299	    )
300	    if not hmac.compare_digest(expected_hash, bytes(entry.entry_hash)):
301	        raise ValueError("entry.entry_hash does not match the envelope digest")
302	    aad = _seal_aad(entry.index, previous_hash)
303	    try:
304	        return AESGCM(key).decrypt(nonce, sealed, aad)
305	    except InvalidTag as error:
306	        raise ValueError("AEAD authentication failed: wrong key or corrupted entry") from error
307	
308	
309	def _hash_parts(hash_name: str, *parts: bytes) -> bytes:
310	    digest = hashlib.new(hash_name)
311	    for part in parts:
312	        digest.update(part)
313	    return digest.digest()
314	
315	
316	def _evolve_key(key: bytes, hash_name: str) -> bytes:
317	    """Derive the next-stage key; the predecessor key is discarded."""
318	    return _hash_parts(hash_name, _EVOLVE_DOMAIN, key)
319	
320	
321	def _locator_digest(payload: bytes, hash_name: str) -> bytes:
322	    """Content digest used only to locate candidate entries in the index."""
323	    return _hash_parts(hash_name, _LOCATE_DOMAIN, payload)
324	
325	
326	def _encrypted_locator_digest(key: bytes, payload: bytes, hash_name: str) -> bytes:
327	    """Keyed locator digest of an encrypted entry's original plaintext.
328	
329	    ``HMAC(key, b"auditchain/encrypted-locate/v1\\0" || payload)``: only a
330	    holder of the append-time key can compute a candidate, and neither the
331	    plaintext nor the key is stored in the index.
332	    """
333	    return hmac.new(key, _ENC_LOCATE_DOMAIN + payload, hash_name).digest()
334	
335	
336	def _auth_tag(stage: int, entry_hash: bytes, key: bytes, hash_name: str) -> bytes:
337	    return hmac.new(
338	        key,
339	        _AUTH_DOMAIN + stage.to_bytes(_INDEX_BYTES, "big") + entry_hash,
340	        hash_name,
341	    ).digest()
342	
343	
344	def _leaf_hash(entry_hash: bytes, hash_name: str) -> bytes:
345	    return _hash_parts(hash_name, _LEAF_DOMAIN, entry_hash)
346	
347	
348	def _node_hash(left: bytes, right: bytes, hash_name: str) -> bytes:
349	    return _hash_parts(hash_name, _NODE_DOMAIN, left, right)
350	
351	
352	def _next_level(level: list[bytes], hash_name: str) -> list[bytes]:
353	    """Combine adjacent pairs; an odd trailing node is promoted unchanged."""
354	    combined = [
355	        _node_hash(level[index], level[index + 1], hash_name)
356	        for index in range(0, len(level) - 1, 2)
357	    ]
358	    if len(level) % 2:
359	        combined.append(level[-1])
360	    return combined
361	
362	
363	def _root_of(leaves: list[bytes], hash_name: str) -> bytes:
364	    if not leaves:
365	        return _hash_parts(hash_name, _EMPTY_DOMAIN)
366	    level = leaves
367	    while len(level) > 1:
368	        level = _next_level(level, hash_name)
369	    return level[0]
370	
371	
372	def _split_point(n: int) -> int:
373	    """Largest power of two strictly smaller than ``n`` (n >= 2)."""
374	    k = 1 << (n.bit_length() - 1)
375	    return k >> 1 if k == n else k
376	
377	
378	def _subproof(m: int, leaves: list[bytes], complete: bool, hash_name: str) -> list[bytes]:
379	    """RFC 6962 section 2.1.2 SUBPROOF over ``leaves`` (length n >= m >= 1).
380	
381	    ``complete`` marks whether the root of the first ``m`` leaves is already
382	    known to the verifier of the enclosing proof.
383	    """
384	    n = len(leaves)
385	    if m == n:
386	        return [] if complete else [_root_of(leaves, hash_name)]
387	    k = _split_point(n)
388	    if m <= k:
389	        return _subproof(m, leaves[:k], complete, hash_name) + [_root_of(leaves[k:], hash_name)]
390	    return _subproof(m - k, leaves[k:], False, hash_name) + [_root_of(leaves[:k], hash_name)]
391	
392	
393	def _subproof_length(m: int, n: int, complete: bool) -> int:
394	    """Node count of ``_subproof`` for sizes only (0 < m <= n)."""
395	    if m == n:
396	        return 0 if complete else 1
397	    k = _split_point(n)
398	    if m <= k:
399	        return _subproof_length(m, k, complete) + 1
400	    return _subproof_length(m - k, n - k, False) + 1
401	
402	
403	@dataclass(frozen=True)
404	class Entry:
405	    """One immutable log record."""
406	
407	    index: int
408	    payload: bytes
409	    previous_hash: bytes
410	    entry_hash: bytes
411	
412	
413	@dataclass(frozen=True)
414	class PruneReceipt:
415	    """Sealed checkpoint for a verifiable prefix prune.
416	
417	    Captures everything a later :meth:`AuditLog.prune` must agree with before
418	    the payloads of the first ``size`` entries may be released:
419	
420	    - ``hash_name``: hash algorithm of the log that sealed the prefix,
421	    - ``size``: number of entries in the sealed prefix,
422	    - ``merkle_root``: Merkle root of the prefix,
423	    - ``chain_hash``: entry hash of the last prefix entry (the predecessor
424	      digest the first retained entry must carry); a digest-width zero
425	      predecessor for an empty prefix (``GENESIS_HASH`` under sha256).
426	    """
427	
428	    hash_name: str
429	    size: int
430	    merkle_root: bytes
431	    chain_hash: bytes
432	
433	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
434	        if not isinstance(self.hash_name, str):
435	            raise TypeError("hash_name must be a string")
436	        if not isinstance(self.size, int) or isinstance(self.size, bool):
437	            raise TypeError("size must be an integer")
438	        if self.size < 0:
439	            raise ValueError("size must be non-negative")
440	        digest_size = _digest_size(self.hash_name)
441	        for name in ("merkle_root", "chain_hash"):
442	            value = getattr(self, name)
443	            if not isinstance(value, (bytes, bytearray)):
444	                raise TypeError(f"{name} must be bytes")
445	            if len(value) != digest_size:
446	                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be {digest_size} bytes")
447	            if not isinstance(value, bytes):
448	                object.__setattr__(self, name, bytes(value))
449	
450	    def matches(self, entry: Any) -> bool:
451	        """Whether ``entry`` is the first record retained after this prefix.
452	
453	        Its absolute index must equal ``size`` and its predecessor digest must
454	        equal ``chain_hash``. A receipt for the empty prefix matches the
455	        genesis record: an entry at index 0 whose predecessor is the
456	        digest-width zero value (``GENESIS_HASH`` under sha256).
457	        """
458	        if not isinstance(entry, Entry):
459	            raise TypeError("entry must be an Entry")
460	        return entry.index == self.size and entry.previous_hash == self.chain_hash
461

463	@dataclass(frozen=True)
464	class AuditReceipt:
465	    """Offline receipt for selected entries of a snapshot.
466	
467	    Issued by :meth:`AuditLog.audit_receipt` and verified entirely offline
468	    by :func:`verify_audit_receipt`:
469	
470	    - ``version``: receipt format version, always ``1``,
471	    - ``hash_name``: hash algorithm of the log that issued the receipt,
472	    - ``size``: number of entries in the snapshot the receipt refers to,
473	    - ``root``: Merkle root of that snapshot,
474	    - ``items``: ``(Entry, proof)`` pairs in ascending absolute index order,
475	      where ``proof`` is the tuple of sibling digests of the entry's

477	      snapshot carries its last entry (index ``size - 1``) with its inclusion
478	      proof; only an empty snapshot (``size == 0``) carries ``items == ()``,
479	      and an empty snapshot never carries any items.

483	    hash_name: str

488	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:

490	            raise TypeError("version must be an integer")
491	        if self.version != 1:
492	            raise ValueError("version must be 1")
493	        if not isinstance(self.hash_name, str):
494	            raise TypeError("hash_name must be a string")
495	        digest_size = _digest_size(self.hash_name)
496	        if not isinstance(self.size, int) or isinstance(self.size, bool):
497	            raise TypeError("size must be an integer")
498	        if self.size < 0:
499	            raise ValueError("size must be non-negative")
500	        if not isinstance(self.root, (bytes, bytearray)):
501	            raise TypeError("root must be bytes")
502	        if len(self.root) != digest_size:
503	            raise ValueError(f"root must be {digest_size} bytes")
504	        if not isinstance(self.root, bytes):

506	        if not isinstance(self.items, tuple):

510	            if not isinstance(item, tuple) or len(item) != 2:
511	                raise TypeError("each item must be an (Entry, proof) tuple")
512	            entry, proof = item
513	            if not isinstance(entry, Entry):

515	            if not isinstance(entry.index, int) or isinstance(entry.index, bool):
516	                raise TypeError("entry.index must be an integer")
517	            if entry.index < 0:

519	            for name in ("payload", "previous_hash", "entry_hash"):

522	            if len(entry.previous_hash) != digest_size:
523	                raise ValueError(f"entry.previous_hash must be {digest_size} bytes")
524	            if len(entry.entry_hash) != digest_size:

527	                raise ValueError("item indices must be in strictly ascending order")
528	            previous_index = entry.index
529	            if not isinstance(proof, tuple):
530	                raise TypeError("item proof must be a tuple of digests")

532	                if not isinstance(sibling, (bytes, bytearray)):
533	                    raise TypeError("proof element must be bytes")
534	                if len(sibling) != digest_size:

541	            # index size - 1 with its inclusion proof; an items==() receipt
542	            # for size > 0 would attest to an arbitrary root with no
543	            # evidence at all and must never be constructible.
544	            raise ValueError(

546	                "at index size - 1"

568	    fields.

719	            )

730	class IntegrityReport:
731	    """Result of :meth:`AuditLog.verify_report`.
732	
733	    ``issues`` holds :class:`IntegrityIssue` values in ascending absolute
734	    index order; the entry-independent ``("head", None)`` issue, when present,
735	    is the trailing element. ``ok`` is the single source of truth and is
736	    ``True`` exactly when ``issues`` is empty. Reports compare by their fields
737	    (``ok`` and ``issues`` only) and may be built positionally.
738	    """

740	    ok: bool
741	    issues: tuple
742	
743	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
744	        if not isinstance(self.ok, bool):
745	            raise TypeError("ok must be a bool")
746	        if not isinstance(self.issues, tuple):
747	            raise TypeError("issues must be a tuple")
748	        for issue in self.issues:
749	            if not isinstance(issue, IntegrityIssue):
750	                raise TypeError("each issue must be an IntegrityIssue")
751	        rank = {
752	            _ISSUE_INDEX: 0,
753	            _ISSUE_PREVIOUS_HASH: 1,
754	            _ISSUE_ENTRY_HASH: 2,
755	            _ISSUE_HEAD: 3,
756	        }
757	
758	        def order_key(issue: IntegrityIssue) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
759	            # The index-less "head" issue sorts after every indexed position.
760	            if issue.code == _ISSUE_HEAD:
761	                return (1, 0, rank[_ISSUE_HEAD])
762	            return (0, issue.index, rank[issue.code])  # type: ignore[arg-type]
763	
764	        previous_key: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None
765	        for position, issue in enumerate(self.issues):
766	            if issue.code == _ISSUE_HEAD and position != len(self.issues) - 1:
767	                raise ValueError("a 'head' issue may only be the final issue")
768	            key = order_key(issue)
769	            if previous_key is not None and key <= previous_key:
770	                raise ValueError(
771	                    "issues must be in ascending index order, with codes "
772	                    "'index', 'previous_hash', 'entry_hash' at one position"
773	                )
774	            previous_key = key
775	        if self.ok != (len(self.issues) == 0):
776	            raise ValueError("ok must be True exactly when issues is empty")

779	class AuditLog:
780	    """Append-only hash chain held in memory.

782	    A pruned log keeps only entries from ``retain_from`` onward. Absolute
783	    indices, the chain head and every rebuildable Merkle snapshot stay
784	    identical to an unpruned log holding the same records; snapshots wholly
785	    inside a pruned prefix can no longer be produced.

789	        digest_size = _digest_size(hash_name)
790	        genesis = bytes(digest_size)
791	        if key is not None:
792	            if not isinstance(key, bytes):
793	                raise TypeError("key must be bytes")
794	            if len(key) == 0:
795	                raise ValueError("key must be non-empty")
796	        self._hash_name = hash_name
797	        self._digest_size = digest_size
798	        self._entries: list[Entry] = []
799	        self._retain_from = 0
800	        self._head: bytes = genesis

802	        # indices of the retained entries carrying that digest. Digests only
803	        # narrow the candidates; find() always re-compares the stored payload.
804	        self._index: dict[bytes, list[int]] = {}
805	        # Keyed locator index for find_encrypted(): HMAC over the original
806	        # plaintext -> ascending absolute indices of retained encrypted
807	        # entries. Holds neither plaintext nor keys; a hit is always confirmed
808	        # by decrypting with the query key and byte-comparing the plaintext.
809	        self._encrypted_index: dict[bytes, list[int]] = {}
810	        # Reverse map (absolute index -> its locator digest) so a prune can
811	        # drop released encrypted entries from _encrypted_index without the
812	        # append-time key; only retained entries are present.
813	        self._encrypted_locators: dict[int, bytes] = {}
814	        # Chain hash of the last pruned entry (the digest_size-byte zero
815	        # predecessor before any prune).
816	        self._checkpoint_head: bytes = genesis
817	        # Roots of the maximal perfect subtrees covering [0, retain_from),
818	        # keyed by subtree height (a subtree of height h holds 2**h leaves).
819	        self._frontier: dict[int, bytes] = {}
820	        # Forward-secure authentication state. ``key is None`` is keyless
821	        # mode: the authentication interface is disabled.
822	        self._key: bytes | None = key
823	        self._stage = 0
824	        self._verifier_exported = False
825	        # Tags of retained entries, keyed by absolute index.
826	        self._tags: dict[int, AuthTag] = {}
827	        # Nonces already used by encrypt(); retained for the log's whole
828	        # lifetime, including across prunes, so a nonce can never repeat
829	        # under the same log even after its envelope has been released.
830	        self._used_nonces: set[bytes] = set()

832	    @property
833	    def hash_name(self) -> str:
834	        return self._hash_name
835	
836	    @property
837	    def retain_from(self) -> int:
838	        """Absolute index of the first entry still held after the last prune."""
839	        return self._retain_from
840	
841	    def __len__(self) -> int:
842	        return self._retain_from + len(self._entries)

844	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[Entry]:

847	    @property
848	    def head(self) -> bytes:

851	    def append(self, payload: Any) -> Entry:
852	        material = _as_bytes(payload)
853	        index = len(self)
854	        entry = Entry(
855	            index=index,
856	            payload=material,
857	            previous_hash=self._head,
858	            entry_hash=entry_digest(index, self._head, material, hash_name=self._hash_name),
859	        )
860	        self._entries.append(entry)
861	        self._index.setdefault(_locator_digest(material, self._hash_name), []).append(index)

865	    def encrypt(self, payload: Any, key: Any, nonce: Any = None) -> Entry:
866	        """Append an AES-256-GCM-encrypted entry.

869	        index, predecessor link and entry digest follow the same rules — but
870	        the stored ``Entry.payload`` is a self-describing envelope rather than
871	        the plaintext:
872	
873	        ``b"auditchain/encrypted-entry/v1\\0" || 0x01 || nonce (12) ||
874	        ciphertext || tag (16)``.
875	
876	        The GCM additional authenticated data binds the ciphertext to its
877	        chain position:
878	
879	        ``b"auditchain/aead/v1\\0" || 0x01 || index (u64 big-endian) ||
880	        previous_hash``.
881	
882	        ``key`` must be 32 ``bytes`` and is never stored; ``nonce`` must be
883	        12 ``bytes`` and must never repeat within this log (history is kept
884	        for the log's lifetime, including after prunes). When ``nonce`` is
885	        ``None`` a fresh ``os.urandom(12)`` nonce is generated. The envelope
886	        itself is what participates in :func:`entry_digest`; use the
887	        top-level :func:`decrypt_entry` to recover the plaintext. Any failure
888	        raises before the log is touched, leaving all state unchanged.
889	        """

891	        _check_key(key)
892	        if nonce is None:
893	            nonce = os.urandom(_NONCE_BYTES)
894	        else:
895	            _check_nonce(nonce)
896	            if nonce in self._used_nonces:
897	                raise ValueError("nonce has already been used in this log")
898	        # Also defend against the astronomically unlikely random collision.
899	        while nonce in self._used_nonces:
900	            nonce = os.urandom(_NONCE_BYTES)

902	        previous_hash = self._head
903	        aad = _seal_aad(index, previous_hash)

908	        # neither the plaintext nor the key.

910	            key, material, self._hash_name

913	        # plaintext locator entry. Nothing before this point mutates the log,
914	        # so a failed encrypt leaves both indexes untouched.
915	        entry = Entry(
916	            index=index,
917	            payload=envelope,
918	            previous_hash=previous_hash,
919	            entry_hash=entry_digest(index, previous_hash, envelope, hash_name=self._hash_name),
920	        )
921	        self._entries.append(entry)
922	        self._index.setdefault(_locator_digest(envelope, self._hash_name), []).append(index)
923	        self._encrypted_index.setdefault(encrypted_locator, []).append(index)
924	        self._encrypted_locators[index] = encrypted_locator
925	        self._used_nonces.add(nonce)

1128	    def verify_report(self) -> IntegrityReport:
1129	        """Verify the retained chain, locating every mismatch in the result.
1130	
1131	        Walks the retained entries forward from the prune checkpoint — the
1132	        digest-width zero predecessor for an unpruned or empty log, the sealed
1133	        checkpoint after a prune. At each expected absolute index the entry
1134	        digest is recomputed as
1135	        ``H(b"auditchain/entry/v1" || index (u64 big-endian) ||
1136	        previous_recomputed || payload)`` with the log's own hash algorithm
1137	        and digest width, and compared against the recorded index,
1138	        predecessor and entry digest. After the walk the final recomputed
1139	        digest must equal the recorded :attr:`head`.
1140	
1141	        Structurally valid data that simply does not match is collected as
1142	        :class:`IntegrityIssue` records with ``ok=False`` rather than raised:
1143	        at one position the codes appear in the order ``"index"``,
1144	        ``"previous_hash"``, ``"entry_hash"``; a head mismatch appends the
1145	        trailing ``("head", None)``. Issues are listed in ascending absolute
1146	        index order. Walking always continues with the *expected* index and
1147	        the *recomputed* predecessor, so later damage is diagnosed even after
1148	        an earlier mismatch. Illegal fields still raise TypeError or
1149	        ValueError exactly as elsewhere (a non-``Entry`` record, an index that
1150	        is not a non-bool non-negative integer, a non-bytes field, or a
1151	        predecessor/entry digest of the wrong width); such structural
1152	        corruption is reported as an exception, never as an issue. The call is
1153	        read-only.
1154	        """
1155	        issues: list[IntegrityIssue] = []
1156	        previous = self._checkpoint_head
1157	        for offset, entry in enumerate(self._entries):
1158	            index = self._retain_from + offset
1159	            if not isinstance(entry, Entry):
1160	                raise TypeError("entry must be an Entry")
1161	            if not isinstance(entry.index, int) or isinstance(entry.index, bool):
1162	                raise TypeError("entry.index must be an integer")
1163	            if entry.index < 0:
1164	                raise ValueError("entry.index must be non-negative")
1165	            for name in ("payload", "previous_hash", "entry_hash"):
1166	                if not isinstance(getattr(entry, name), (bytes, bytearray)):
1167	                    raise TypeError(f"entry.{name} must be bytes")
1168	            if len(entry.previous_hash) != self._digest_size:
1169	                raise ValueError(
1170	                    f"entry.previous_hash must be {self._digest_size} bytes"
1171	                )
1172	            if len(entry.entry_hash) != self._digest_size:
1173	                raise ValueError(
1174	                    f"entry.entry_hash must be {self._digest_size} bytes"
1175	                )
1176	            if entry.index != index:
1177	                issues.append(IntegrityIssue(_ISSUE_INDEX, index))
1178	            if entry.previous_hash != previous:
1179	                issues.append(IntegrityIssue(_ISSUE_PREVIOUS_HASH, index))
1180	            recomputed = entry_digest(
1181	                index, previous, bytes(entry.payload), hash_name=self._hash_name
1182	            )
1183	            if entry.entry_hash != recomputed:
1184	                issues.append(IntegrityIssue(_ISSUE_ENTRY_HASH, index))
1185	            previous = recomputed
1186	        if previous != self._head:
1187	            issues.append(IntegrityIssue(_ISSUE_HEAD, None))
1188	        return IntegrityReport(ok=not issues, issues=tuple(issues))
